items.title: 56679_Arthur Briggs oral history interview
items.q: his piano player, at the time he was a terrific musician, by the name of Pierre de Caillaux

ctx.x: good colored Dixieland band. The only thing that was good about them was the name. (Laughter). That's why I'm concerned.

You need to listen to Bechet. He would be opposite with the Jazz Kings, Benny Peyton's Jazz Kings, and his piano player, at the time he was a terrific musician, by the name of Pierre de Caillaux, and he was French Canadian, and he, Bechet would, after a number, he would go to Caillaux and say, 'You changed the harmony in this, that spot, and that spot, and that spot.' Caillaux, then after an argument would say, 'Yes, you're right, I did not play the harmony.'
